BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material term. Several items would breach our hard limits, including the fraud carve-out, Fundamental/Title protection, and the Bluefen and Riverlark conditions. Nothing here should be accepted as "agreed," "final," or "market standard." The Seller's own label "Key Negotiated Positions" does not clear anything. Under playbook §0.4/§6.3, these positions need to go through our own authority process.

## 1. Departures from playbook

| # | Topic | Seller position | Playbook position | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start. 20% is a conditional fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written authority, none given | Reject. Restore 25% / AUD 6m. The figure matching our fallback does not clear it. |
| 2 | De minimis / basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket, excess only | AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k basket, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject all three. A deductible basket also strips out the first AUD 250k of claims. |
| 3 | General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months needs Frost approval | Reject. Restore 24 months. |
| 4 | Scope of limitations (cl 13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. This would pull title and tax/IP into the general regime. |
| 5 | Fundamental / Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. "Administrative simplicity" is not a basis for this. |
| 6 | Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable; not waivable | Reject. The fraud carve-out is non-negotiable. |
| 7 | Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records are disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Reject. Require specific disclosure against specific warranties. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject. This is effectively a sandbagging bar on every claim. |
| 9 | Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reject. Note DL §2 confirms no final consent exists. |
| 10 | Riverlark (cl 2/7) | Release to follow Completion; approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Reject. DL §3 confirms the facility is not repaid. |
| 11 | Employee bonuses (funds flow) | AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller," not itemised | Specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; not silently excluded | Reject. Require itemisation and seller funding. |
| 12 | Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure | Reject the narrowing. The AUD 180k is not independently verified. |
| 13 | DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand | Do not accept the materiality characterisation. Require the investigation and updates. |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Do not accept the characterisation. Require the assessment. |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | Reject. Tax and IP stay open and separate. |
| 16 | Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof | Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence (e.g. ASIC extract, searches, transfer documents). |

## 2. Reasoning on the most material issues

**Fundamental/Title and the fraud carve-out (items 5 and 6).** These are the most serious departures. Making title and capacity subject to general caps and short time limits would leave us exposed on the very warranties that define what we are buying. Applying the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature" removes protection for fraud. Our playbook treats both as hard limits, so these should be the first points we press.

**Disclosure and buyer knowledge (items 7 and 8).** Combined, these would mean that almost anything in the data room or on public registers is disclosed against every warranty, and that anything we "could have discovered" cannot be claimed. This would hollow out the general warranty package. The Seller's disclosure letter makes this more serious: §1.1 discloses every fact in the data room "as at 22 September 2026", which is a blanket disclosure, not a specific one.

**Bluefen (item 9).** The consent covers roughly 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m). Treating consent as satisfied on delivery, backed only by reasonable endeavours, means we could complete without knowing whether the conditions in clause 11.3 are met. The playbook requires evidence before Completion.

**Riverlark (item 10).** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and not yet repaid. Releases after Completion are only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval. Without direct repayment from Completion funds, we would be taking on a secured debt position.

**Funds flow and bonuses (item 11).** The AUD 420k in bonuses is excluded from the funds flow. Payroll tax and superannuation on-costs are not quantified. If these are left out, they would fall on the Company post-Completion, which is effectively a price reduction we have not agreed to. The Seller's note that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" is not accepted.

**Ironquay (item 12).** Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay agreement means SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid. The data room has no receipt or confirmatory assignment. The AUD 180k figure comes from DD-010, which is not bank verification either way. The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, which does not cover the broader IP risk.

**DD-006 incident (item 13).** The disclosure does not establish a breach, harm, or notification obligation. It also does not establish that there is no breach. We should not assert either. The right response is preservation of logs, a clear investigation timetable and regular updates. Whether any privacy notification duty arises should be confirmed by privacy counsel, not assumed from the Seller's characterisation.

**Sandbar (item 14).** The "ordinary course" label is the Seller's view. Our playbook requires assessment, not automatic debt treatment or a price deduction. Our response should ask for the termination, accrual and renewal facts, and should not accept the characterisation.

**Stale facts.** All of the disclosure is "as at 22 September 2026." Today is 5 November 2026. Before we respond, the current status of Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment, the DD-006 investigation, and the Sandbar and Mossvale position must be refreshed. We should not rely on the September position.

**Other items.**
- *Mossvale and the office lease (DD-007, DD-009):* The disclosure says the provisions do not expressly require consent for a share sale. That is not the same as confirming no consent is needed. We should ask for a formal legal analysis of each provision.
- *Cross-references:* The clause numbers (for example 2/7, 3/6.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5) do not match a single consistent SPA. We need the full SPA draft to verify them.
- *Non-admission wording (DL §1.4):* The letter says nothing admits that any consent is legally required. We should not treat any of its characterisations as confirmed facts.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the package as a whole.** Do not accept it as "agreed," "final," or "fair and balanced." Tell the Seller that all positions remain open pending our instructions.
2. **Restore the general regime:** 25% / AUD 6m cap; AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k first-dollar tipping basket; 24-month claims period.
3. **Restore Fundamental/Title protection:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Do not allow it to be pulled into the general regime.
4. **Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
5. **Limit disclosure to specific fair disclosure.** Delete the data-room, public-register and Accounts general disclosures in Schedule 7 and DL §1.1–1.2.
6. **Delete the buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3)**, or narrow it to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, with no exclusion for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** Require effective consent and documentary evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is not enough.
8. **Riverlark:** Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval.
9. **Bonuses:** Itemise the AUD 420k and its triggered on-costs in the funds flow, or require the Seller to fund them.
10. **Ironquay:** Broaden the IP indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. Obtain independent evidence of the payment position.
11. **DD-006:** Require log preservation, a documented investigation, a timetable and regular updates. Do not assert breach, harm or any numeric demand. Get privacy counsel's view on notification.
12. **Sandbar:** Require an assessment of each renewal. Do not accept "ordinary course" or any automatic debt or price treatment.
13. **Tax and IP:** Keep them open and separate. Do not accept that they are settled under the general regime.
14. **Title:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is not sufficient on its own.
15. **Mossvale and office lease:** Obtain formal legal advice on whether consent is required, rather than accepting the disclosure's wording.
16. **Refresh all facts** to the current date and verify all clause cross-references against the full SPA.
17. **Escalate to Amelia Frost** for any decision on the 20% cap, the 18-month period or any other fallback. No fallback is authorised until she gives written approval identifying the draft.

*Note: This review is based on the Seller's summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA. Privacy-notification, payroll tax, superannuation and NSW-law points should be confirmed by the relevant specialist counsel.*
